stages.title: Intermediate vocabulary
stages.hook: English borrowed thousands of words from Greek. What do you think "philosophy" means in the original parts?
explain: Greek words are often built from parts. Φίλος means "friend" and σοφία means "wisdom", so φιλοσοφία is "love of wisdom". Τηλέφωνο joins τηλε- (far) and φωνή (voice). The ending -της names a man who does something, as in μαθητής (pupil), and -τρια names a woman: μαθήτρια.
Beware of false friends. Γυμνάσιο is not a gym but a lower secondary school (ages about 12 to 15). Learn words in families: υγεία (health), υγιής (healthy), and the greeting γεια.
stages.mnemonic: Tele-phone: far-voice. Learn the parts and you can open many words.

gq.q: What is a γυμνάσιο in Greece?
o: A sports hall and gym only
gq.why: The word comes from ancient gymnasium, but now means a school.

panel.q: Why does the word τηλέφωνο look similar to "telephone"?
o: Greek took it from English in the 20th century only
English took it from Greek parts: far and voice
panel.why: Tele- and phone are Greek roots used in English.

panel.q: Which is the feminine form of μαθητής (pupil)?
panel.why: The feminine ending is -τρια.

panel.q: Why is it helpful to learn Greek roots?
o: Greek has no roots, only whole words that never change
They appear in many English scientific words
panel.why: Roots like bio-, geo- and phone are Greek.

teach.model: Greek words are built from parts: φίλος and σοφία make φιλοσοφία, "love of wisdom". The ending -της names a person who does something. Beware of false friends like γυμνάσιο.

trip.prompt: Find English words from Greek and note two Greek roots.

sources: List of Greek and Latin roots in English

stages.title: Verb forms and time expressions
stages.hook: Greek past tense changes the start of the verb. How would you say "I wrote"?
explain: The simple past (αόριστος) often adds ε- or changes the end: γράφω (I write) becomes έγραψα (I wrote). Διαβάζω becomes διάβασα. The ongoing past is έγραφα (I was writing). So Greek shows the difference between one finished action and a continuing one.

The future is formed with θα: θα γράψω (I will write, once) and θα γράφω (I will be writing, repeatedly). Time words are χθες (yesterday), σήμερα, αύριο, πάντα, συχνά, ποτέ δεν (never) and ήδη (already).
stages.mnemonic: Θα is the future hat: θα + verb.

gq.q: What is the simple past of γράφω?
gq.why: The past takes ε- and the ending -ψα.

gq.q: How do you say "I will read"?
gq.why: Θα plus the verb forms the future.

panel.q: What is the difference between έγραψα and έγραφα?
o: Έγραψα is a completed act; έγραφα is ongoing or repeated
panel.why: Aspect separates the simple and continuous past.

panel.q: Why is Δεν αργεί ποτέ correct?
o: Ποτέ means always, so δεν cancels it
Greek uses δεν together with ποτέ
panel.why: Double negation is standard.

panel.q: What does θα do in θα γράψω?
panel.why: Θα is the future marker.

teach.model: The simple past of γράφω is έγραψα, and the ongoing past is έγραφα. Make the future with θα: θα γράψω. Use time words like χθες, αύριο, πάντα and ποτέ.

points.ask: How do I say the past?
How do I make the future?
Is there a difference between two pasts?

trip.prompt: Find the list of past forms and compare two verbs.

stages.title: Complex sentence introduction
stages.hook: English says "If it rains, we stay home". Does Greek put θα in the if-part too?
explain: A complex sentence joins clauses. Common words are ότι (that), που (who, which), αν (if), όταν (when), αν και (although), για να (in order to), ενώ (while). Example: Ξέρω ότι έχεις δίκιο.

After αν we use a present or a subjunctive-like form and not θα: Αν βρέξει, θα μείνουμε σπίτι. After για να we use the subjunctive: Μαθαίνω ελληνικά για να διαβάζω βιβλία. The word που links a noun to extra information: Το κορίτσι που μένει δίπλα.
stages.mnemonic: Αν has no θα; the result clause carries it.
sentences: I know that you are right.
If it rains, we will stay at home.
I learn Greek to read books.

gq.why: After αν we do not use θα; the main clause has it.

gq.q: What does που mean in Το κορίτσι που μένει δίπλα?

panel.q: Why does για να take a subjunctive form of the verb?
o: It expresses purpose, which is not a plain fact
panel.why: Purpose clauses use να plus the verb in a subjunctive form.

panel.q: Which word expresses contrast?
panel.why: Ενώ can mean while or whereas.

panel.q: Why is it όταν έρθει and not όταν θα έρθει?
o: After όταν for the future Greek uses the subjunctive form without θα
panel.why: Time clauses in the future use the να-form (subjunctive) without θα.

teach.model: Join clauses with ότι, που, αν, όταν, αν και and για να. After αν and όταν there is no θα for future ideas. After για να use the subjunctive.

points.ask: Do I put θα after αν?
How do I say in order to?

trip.prompt: Find examples of conditional sentences and mark the αν clause.

stages.title: Reading short stories
stages.hook: Many fables use talking animals to teach a lesson. Which ancient Greek storyteller is famous for them?
explain: A Greek tale is a παραμύθι. It often begins with Μια φορά κι έναν καιρό, "once upon a time". Animals such as ο λύκος (wolf), η αρκούδα (bear) and η αλεπού (fox) appear often.

The ancient storyteller Aesop (Αίσωπος) is known for short fables with a moral. In stories the imperfect shows what used to be: Ζούσε μια αλεπού (There lived a fox). Aorist (simple past) verbs show events that happened one after another.
stages.mnemonic: Μια φορά κι έναν καιρό: the magic door of a tale.
sentences: Once upon a time there lived a fox.
The wolf lived in the forest.

gq.q: How does a Greek tale often begin?
gq.why: It is the Greek "once upon a time".

gq.q: Who is associated with famous animal fables?
gq.why: Aesop is the traditional author of fables with a moral.

panel.q: Why do fables use animals?
o: Animals can show human faults or virtues in a simple, safe way
panel.why: Animals stand for human traits.

panel.q: What does ζούσε (imperfect) tell us about the fox?
o: It lived only for one short moment in the story
It lived there for some time as background
panel.why: The imperfect describes continuing past situations.

panel.q: A story ends with Αυτό είναι το τέλος. What word is τέλος?
panel.why: Τέλος means end.

teach.model: Greek tales start with Μια φορά κι έναν καιρό. They use the past tense, and animals such as the fox and the wolf are common. Aesop is the famous ancient fable teller.

trip.prompt: Read one fable and say its moral in one sentence.

stages.title: Listening comprehension
stages.hook: In Greek, ι, η, υ, ει and οι sound the same. How do you know which letter to write when you listen?
explain: Useful verbs: ακούω (I hear, I listen), προσέχω (I pay attention), καταλαβαίνω (I understand). Words for speed and loudness: δυνατά (loudly), σιγά (quietly), γρήγορα (quickly), αργά (slowly).

Because several letters sound alike, listeners must know spelling from reading. Some pairs of words sound the same but are written differently: η (the) and ή (or) differ only by the accent. Listen for stress and context, not for letters.
stages.mnemonic: Ears hear "i", eyes decide the letter.
sentences: I hear but I do not understand.

gq.q: What is the difference between η and ή?
o: Both mean the, but in different cases
gq.why: The accent separates two words that sound alike.

panel.q: Why can Greek dictation be hard?
o: Several letters share one sound, so spelling must be learned
panel.why: Homophones need spelling knowledge.

panel.q: Which strategy helps with fast speech?
o: Check every letter of every word
panel.why: Meaning comes from stressed words and context.

panel.q: Why does the accent matter in writing και ή?
o: It can separate words that sound the same
panel.why: Accents help the reader.

teach.model: Several Greek letters sound alike, so listen for stress and context. Some words differ only by the accent, like η and ή. Ask Ξανά, παρακαλώ if needed.

trip.prompt: Find the list of homophones and read three pairs aloud.

stages.title: Conversation and pronunciation
stages.hook: The letter γ sounds different before different vowels. How do you say γεια?
explain: The letter γ is a soft rough sound before α, ο, ου, but before ε and ι it sounds like "y": γεια is "ya". The letters δ and θ are different sounds: δ is like "th" in "this" and θ is like "th" in "think".
Intonation: a statement falls and a yes/no question rises. Practise phrases aloud. A common phrase is Επανάλαβε μετά από μένα (repeat after me). Do not fear mistakes.
stages.mnemonic: Γεια: the γ turns into y before ε and ι.
sentences: Do not be afraid of mistakes.

gq.q: How is γ pronounced in γεια?
gq.why: Before ε and ι, γ sounds like y.
Θ is voiceless, δ is voiced.

panel.q: Why is δ different from θ?
o: Δ is voiced (like "this") and θ is voiceless (like "think")
panel.why: Voiced and voiceless "th" are separate letters.

panel.q: Why are speaking and repetition important?
o: Sounds are learned with the ear and mouth, not eyes only
panel.why: Imitation builds pronunciation.

panel.q: Which word is said with a y-like sound?
panel.why: Γ before ε/ι: ya.

teach.model: Before ε and ι the letter γ sounds like y, as in γεια. Δ is like "th" in "this" and θ is like "th" in "think". Practise by repeating aloud.

points.ask: How are δ and θ different?

trip.prompt: Find the table of consonants and read the sound of γ, δ and θ.

stages.title: Writing paragraphs
stages.hook: Greek has a raised dot that works like a semicolon. Have you seen it?
explain: A paragraph is built from linking words: πρώτα (first), μετά (then), ύστερα (afterwards), έπειτα (next), τέλος (finally). Add ideas with εκτός από αυτό (besides) and examples with για παράδειγμα.

Introductory words are separated by commas: Τέλος, γυρίσαμε σπίτι. Greek uses ; as a question mark and a raised dot (·), called άνω τελεία, for a pause like the English semicolon. A formal letter begins Αξιότιμε κύριε (Dear Sir).
stages.mnemonic: Πρώτα, μετά, τέλος: first, then, finally.
sentences: First I read, then I write.

gq.q: Which Greek mark works like an English semicolon?
gq.why: The άνω τελεία marks a pause.

gq.q: How does a formal letter to a man start?

panel.q: Why use words like πρώτα and μετά?
o: They change the tense of the verb
They show the order of ideas
panel.why: Linking words guide the reader.

panel.q: What does a paragraph need?
o: One main idea supported by its sentences
panel.why: A paragraph has unity.

panel.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
panel.why: A comma follows the introductory word.

teach.model: Link sentences with πρώτα, μετά and τέλος. Separate introductory words with a comma. Remember that ; is a question mark and · is a pause.

points.ask: Which marks are special in Greek?

trip.prompt: Find the question mark and the raised dot and copy one sentence with each.

stages.title: Cultural expressions and idioms
stages.hook: In Greek "It is raining chair legs" means something very ordinary. What?
explain: Idioms are fixed expressions. Βρέχει καρεκλοπόδαρα (it rains chair legs) means it is raining heavily. Έπεσα από τα σύννεφα (I fell from the clouds) means I was very surprised. Κάνω την πάπια (I do the duck) means to pretend not to understand.
Some set phrases are used at special moments. Καλή όρεξη! is said before a meal, Στην υγειά μας! is a toast and Καλή επιτυχία! wishes success. Όποιος σπέρνει, θερίζει means "you reap what you sow".
stages.mnemonic: Chair legs from the sky: it is pouring.

gq.q: What do you say before a meal?
gq.why: It is the Greek "enjoy your meal".

gq.q: What does Έπεσα από τα σύννεφα mean?
o: I was cold and wet from the rain
gq.why: The idiom is about sudden surprise.

panel.q: Why can you not translate Βρέχει καρεκλοπόδαρα word by word?
o: It is an idiom with its own meaning
It is a verb only, with no other words
panel.why: Idioms have a fixed figurative meaning.

panel.q: What does Όποιος σπέρνει, θερίζει teach?
panel.why: You get what you plant.

panel.q: Which phrase fits a toast?
panel.why: It literally means to our health.

teach.model: Idioms have their own meaning, like Έπεσα από τα σύννεφα for surprise. Use Καλή όρεξη before meals and Στην υγειά μας for a toast.

points.ask: What do I say before eating?
What do I say for a toast?

trip.prompt: Pick one proverb and explain it in your own words.

stages.title: Practical travel communication
stages.hook: On a Greek road sign you see Έξοδος. Do you go in or out?
explain: Travel words are σταθμός (station), αεροδρόμιο (airport), εισιτήριο (ticket), διαβατήριο (passport), ξενοδοχείο (hotel), δωμάτιο (room), χάρτης (map) and στάση (stop). Signs: Είσοδος (entrance), Έξοδος (exit), Ταμείο (cashier).

To ask directions say Πού είναι ο σταθμός; or Πώς πάω στο ξενοδοχείο; To buy a ticket say Ένα εισιτήριο για την Αθήνα, παρακαλώ. After για use the accusative: για την Αθήνα. With strangers ask politely: Συγγνώμη, ξέρετε πού είναι...;
stages.mnemonic: Είσοδος starts like "is-in", έξοδος has the ξ of "ex-it".
sentences: How do I get to the hotel?

gq.q: What does the sign Έξοδος mean?
gq.why: Έξοδος means exit and είσοδος means entrance.
Για takes the accusative: την Αθήνα.

panel.q: Why should you learn to read Greek signs?
o: All signs in Greece are always also in English
Many local signs only use Greek letters
panel.why: Reading the alphabet helps you travel.

panel.q: Why is Συγγνώμη, ξέρετε...; polite?
o: Ξέρετε is rude and too direct here
panel.why: The -ετε ending shows politeness.

panel.q: Why does a place name look different on a map in Latin letters?
o: Names are transliterated, so spellings vary
panel.why: Αθήνα may appear as Athina or Athens.

teach.model: Learn σταθμός, εισιτήριο, διαβατήριο and ξενοδοχείο, and signs like Είσοδος and Έξοδος. Ask Πού είναι...; and say για with the accusative.

points.ask: How do I ask where something is?

trip.prompt: Look at a map of Athens and read three place names in Greek.
